::: proof
In @sec-est-LMs,
setting the score equal to zero showed that $\evb$ solves
$\tp{\mX}\mX\evb = \tp{\mX}\vy$.
Then:

$$
\ba
\tp{\mX}\vresid
&= \tp{\mX}\paren{\vy - \mX\evb}
&& \text{(definition of } \vresid \text{ and } \hat{\vy} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\mX}\vy - \tp{\mX}\mX\evb
&& \text{(distribute } \tp{\mX} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\mX}\vy - \tp{\mX}\vy
&& \text{(} \evb \text{ solves the score equation)}
\\
&= \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

If the model has an intercept,
the first column of $\mX$ is all ones,
so the first entry of @eq-ols-resid-orthogonal is $\sumin 1 \cdot \resid_i = 0$.
For the fitted values:

$$
\ba
\sumin \hat y_i \resid_i
&= \tp{\hat{\vy}} \vresid
&& \text{(sum of products as an inner product)}
\\
&= \tp{\paren{\mX\evb}} \vresid
&& \text{(definition of } \hat{\vy} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\evb} \tp{\mX} \vresid
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \tp{\evb} \mathbf{0}_{(p+1) \times 1}
&& \text{(the orthogonality just shown)}
\\
&= 0
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$
:::
